findings.F1: The book earns on its long side. Long bars give 10.54 bps per day of the book's 10.47 gross, and short bars give −0.08. By trade, long trades sum to +16,726 % (1,792 trades) and short trades to −1,486 % (1,238). Short trades entered more than 30 % below the 60-day high lose −1,906 % (mean −5.0 %, 33 % winners).
findings.F2: The gain comes from a few long trends. The top 5 % of the 3,030 trades make 110 % of the net sum, and 45 % of trades win. The top 30 long trades make 59 % of the long sum and fall in only 5 windows. Of those 30, 25 are XRP (14) or ZEC (11), and their median hold is 42 days.
findings.F3: The market's own rise is a minor part of the gain: 2.73 of the 10.47 bps per day gross, with 7.74 bps of timing. Timing is spread over the years but turns negative in 2022 (−0.41) and 2023 (−1.21). By window, gross gain runs from −0.43 to +1.99 bps, and 8 of 24 windows lose.
findings.F4: The book earns where the coin is near its 60-day high, and the 10-day move falls in step with the distance below it. Long contribution is 3.24, 2.84, 2.08, 0.60 and 0.45 bps per day from "at the high" to "more than 30 % below". Over the next 10 days, on the non-overlapping grid, the excess return is +2.08 % (n 122), +1.67 % (194), +0.39 % (399), −0.96 % (376) and −0.70 % (312). Nearness alone has a slope t of 1.63 (n 1,403).
findings.F5: The test measured a standardised forecast, and that hides the idea. On the 10-day grid, the forecast has a slope t of 1.01 and the recorded component, standardised against its own past 60 values, 1.04. The plain level of the 28-day return times (1/(1+D))² has a slope t of 2.69 (n 1,259), above the 28-day return alone (t 2.29).
findings.F6: Among coins whose 28-day return is positive, nearness to the 60-day high grades the next 10-day move (t 1.69, n 644). The largest cell is the top quarter of 28-day returns at the high: +4.36 % excess over 10 days (n 79).
findings.F7: At shorter horizons the forecast predicts better than at the plan's 10 days, and the move fades beyond it. Slope t is 2.17 at 1 day (n 17,380), 2.12 at 3 days (n 5,723) and 1.09 at 10 days (n 1,691). It is near zero at 20 and 30 days (0.01 and 0.61). The 3-day signed excess return is 0.23 %, barely above the 0.19 % cost of a round trip, while the 10-day unusual move of 1.37 % is 7.1 times that cost.

ideas.idea: The higher a coin's 28-day return multiplied by its nearness to its 60-day closing high (the closer to the high, the larger the weight), the higher its return over the next 10 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader would size long momentum bets by the plain level of the rise scaled by nearness to the high, rather than by how unusual that level is against its own recent past.
ideas.name: momentum level near highs

ideas.idea: The closer a coin's close is to its highest close of the last 60 days, the higher its return over the next 10 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader would hold more of a coin the nearer it trades to its 60-day high, and little of it far below.
ideas.name: nearness to 60-day high

ideas.idea: While a coin's 28-day return is positive, the closer its close is to its 60-day closing high, the larger its return over the next 10 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader would keep a long momentum bet only in proportion to the coin's nearness to its high, and refuse the shorts that lost far below it.
ideas.name: rising coins near highs
